Terra's counterexamples check out from disk: lem-connected-subsets-and-separated-sets argues with relatively open pieces and thm-closure-of-a-connected-set with separated sets, neither with a map to 2. The paragraph is an expository claim about how the page's other proofs are phrased, not a mathematical assertion, and claim 2 in its clopen form genuinely is the criterion those proofs use - claim 1 (b) iff (c) makes the two forms the same test. Nothing rests on it. Recorded: "every later proof" overstates.

The paragraph is a forward-pointing terminology note that defers the actual definition ("it is not defined here because it is stated in terms of components"), and the definition body states four paragraphs above that "The empty space and the one-point space are connected in this library". Degenerate-case paraphrase, recorded.

That half is the standard definition of the closure operator, and the topological closure is already in play through [A5]. Recorded: def-interior-closure-boundary-top should be declared.

Correct that thm-reals-ordered-field is the item proving R is an ordered field and that it is not declared. def-complete-ordered-field IS declared, and it is the item by which this library fixes what R is - def-finite-sum opens "Throughout this page R is the complete ordered field ([[def-complete-ordered-field]])". def-connected-space is declared in deps and states the convention verbatim: "The empty space and the one-point space are connected in this library. Neither admits a separation". [A4]'s restatement dropped it, so step 1.1's empty-product case reads as uncited. Fact-fidelity imprecision on a stated convention.

The passage from "p is not an upper bound of S" to "there is s in S with p < s" is linearity, which [A1] of this very item supplies ("the order is linear, so any two elements are comparable and exactly one of x<y, x=y, y<x holds"). Step 5.1's tag names [A2] only. Tag incompleteness.

Section 3 misstates a named literature notion and describes a vacuous condition as a weaker one. It reads "Dropping the word *open* from V gives a weaker condition at a point, called *connectedness im kleinen* in the literature", but a connected V with x in V contained in U is satisfied by V = {x} for every x and every U, so the stripped condition holds in every space. Connectedness im kleinen at x asks for a connected NEIGHBOURHOOD V of x inside U - a distinction this item's own inherited-conventions paragraph ("a neighbourhood need not be open") makes expressible. Nothing in the item rescues the sentence.

Terra's witness uses a closed initial segment; the item's own usage fixes the strict reading, at line 107: "{0} x [0,1) is an initial segment of R order-isomorphic to [0,1)", which is the set of elements strictly below (1,0). Under that reading the claim holds for every such segment determined by a point above the least element and fails only at the empty one. Recorded: the remark should say "every proper initial segment determined by a point above the least element".

The second clause of [A6] follows from the first in one step: given M, if M <= 0 then 1 > M, and if M > 0 then cor-archimedean-reciprocal at epsilon = 1/M gives k with 1/k < 1/M, hence k > M. The corollary is declared in deps and cited on the same line. A consequence bundled into a Fact rather than derived.

Terra's count is right: the Sierpinski row shares the reason, so five of the six rows are connected because no two nonempty open sets are disjoint, and only the discrete row is not. The Example says so itself, fifteen lines above: "Sierpinski space is the particular-point topology on a two-point set, so its row is an instance of the row above it and is not verified separately". A miscount in explanatory prose, contradicted in advance by the item's own text; every named instance is correct. ESCALATED to the orchestrator as a fourth finding on this item; the one-word correction "Four" to "Five" is recommended but is not a fatal repair and R1 does not license it here.

note: def-complete-ordered-field states the invoked property verbatim - 'F is a complete ordered field (equivalently, F has the least-upper-bound property...) if every nonempty S subset of F that is bounded above has a least upper bound in F' - so the citation names exactly the axiom step uses. That R has it is established, not assumed: library/real-analysis/foundations-of-the-real-numbers.md adopts the complete-ordered-field abstraction only after both constructions are shown to satisfy the axioms ('Because both constructions are already known to satisfy the axioms', 'The Cauchy model is complete in the [least-upper-bound] sense', 'the Dedekind model is a complete ordered field by construction'), with cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete supplying the Cauchy half. Every published item in this development cites def-complete-ordered-field for this move in the same way (thm-nth-roots-exist's Given, def-finite-sum's opening sentence, rem-real-exponents-deferred). The context_sha256 is the current pair-context hash computed from disk at adjudication time; the item is unchanged since the post-realpower-repair snapshot. An earlier independent Alpha reached the same disposition on the pre-repair text (research/frontier-7-judge-adjudications.jsonl).

New finding on the A8-repaired text, unrelated to the repair: step 1.2 multiplies two positive roots without a cited closure fact. Closure of the positives under multiplication is an ordered-field axiom, and this item declares thm-rat-ordered-field and uses lem-of-inverse-positive from the same ordered-field vocabulary; lem-power-monotone's own [L3] in this item already states 'a product of positives is positive' as the sign rule it rests on. A one-line ordered-field move. R1: closed on this row with no edit.

New finding on the A8-repaired text, in section 2 rather than the repaired section 3, and Terra is right. Section 2 claims 'disjoint open sets in a subspace need not be separated in the ambient space'. They always are: if U, V are disjoint and open in S, write V = W ∩ S with W open in X; then W ∩ U ⊆ W ∩ S = V and U ∩ V = ∅ give W ∩ U = ∅, so V misses the closure of U in X, and symmetrically. The item's own cited lem-connected-subsets-and-separated-sets runs exactly that argument at its step 3.1. The true distinction, which def-connected-space states, is that the AMBIENT open sets witnessing a separation of a subspace need only be disjoint ON the subspace: 'it asks U and V to be disjoint on A, not in X. Requiring U ∩ V = ∅ outright is a strictly stronger demand and is a different notion.' Repaired to state that.
